competitors.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: How AWS Built an Enterprise Platform for AI Agent Deployment
key_points: AgentCore is five tightly integrated services: Runtime, Gateway, Memory, Identity, and Observability
Runtime: serverless compute at $0.0895/vCPU-hour, billed per second, idle time free
Gateway: managed MCP server at $0.005/1,000 invocations, handles OAuth credential management
Memory: short-term ($0.25/1,000 events) and long-term persistence across sessions
Identity: agent-level IAM with Okta, Entra, or Cognito integration
Framework-agnostic: supports LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK
Epsilon reported 30% faster campaign setup, 20% more personalization after deploying on AgentCore

competitors.title: Policy Overview - Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (Official AWS Docs)
key_points: Policy uses Cedar language (AWS open-source authorization language) for fine-grained access control
Cedar uses forbid-overrides-permit evaluation: default deny, forbid wins over permit
Two enforcement modes: LOG_ONLY (test) and ENFORCE (production)
Policies control access based on user identity, OAuth scopes, tool input parameters
Authorization flow: JWT token + MCP tool call -> Cedar evaluation -> ALLOW/DENY
Limitations: no floating-point numbers, no regex, no date/time comparisons, max 1000 policies per engine

competitors.title: Agent Identity in 2026: A Practical Blueprint with Entra Agent ID, AWS AgentCore Policy, A2A/AP2, and MCP
key_points: Microsoft projecting 1.3B AI agents in use by 2028, Entra Agent ID brings first-class identity for agents
10-step rollout: inventory agents, stand up registry, issue identities, define policy-as-code, enforce at gateway
Policy enforcement at gateway intercepts every tool call for auth, authorization, and DLP before execution
AgentCore Evaluations monitor accuracy, tool selection, and helpfulness with SLAs and fail-safes
Governance checklist: every agent needs owner, identity, purpose tag, data classification, and SLA

competitors.title: AWS Config Adds 30 New Resource Types: Bedrock AgentCore Gateways & Memory (2026)

Memory tracking enables audit of retention policy changes, compliance rules for encryption, inventory at scale
Config rules can flag Memory without encryption-at-rest or retention exceeding governance requirements
Governance visibility for agent infrastructure now matches EC2/S3 compliance controls

angles: AgentOps as the new SRE: agents don't fail like chatbots — they fail like distributed systems, requiring tracing, evals, policy gates, and rollback-ready automation
The five-pillar framework: Runtime, Gateway, Memory, Identity, and Observability as the complete AgentOps stack for production agents
Policy-as-code for agents: how Cedar language and natural language authoring give security teams deterministic control without slowing development
Memory metrics that matter: tracking episodic memory effectiveness, cross-session learning rates, and memory compaction efficiency
Gateway observability: monitoring tool invocation patterns, OAuth credential health, and policy enforcement latency at the agent gateway
Identity-driven agent governance: agent-level IAM with Entra Agent ID and Cognito as the foundation for audit trails and compliance
Cost-aware AgentOps: understanding the consumption-based pricing model and optimizing agent infrastructure costs across Runtime, Gateway, and Memory
From prototype to production: the metrics that prove agent reliability — evaluation scores, policy violation rates, memory hit rates, and gateway latency
outline: Introduction: Why AgentOps Matters in 2026 — agents as distributed systems
The Five Pillars of AgentCore: Runtime, Gateway, Memory, Identity, Observability
Policy Metrics: Cedar language, natural language authoring, enforcement modes, and policy evaluation latency
Gateway Metrics: tool invocation counts, OAuth credential health, MCP server availability, and policy enforcement pass/fail rates
Memory Metrics: episodic memory hit rate, cross-session learning effectiveness, memory compaction efficiency, and storage costs
Identity Metrics: agent authentication success rates, IAM role mapping, Entra/Cognito integration health, and audit trail completeness
Observability Metrics: execution trajectory inspection, evaluation scores (correctness, helpfulness, safety), and CloudWatch integration
Cost Tracking: consumption-based pricing breakdown, per-agent cost allocation, and optimization strategies
Config-Driven Governance: AWS Config resource tracking for Gateways and Memory, drift detection, and compliance rules
Comparison with Alternatives: Google ADK, OpenAI Agents SDK, Azure AI Agent Service — where AgentCore wins on infrastructure metrics
Real-World Adoption: Epsilon, Druva, Natera, S&P Global — metrics from production deployments
Setting Up an AgentOps Dashboard: key metrics to track, alert thresholds, and SLO definitions
Future Trends: agent-to-agent protocol metrics, cross-platform agent governance, and the 1.3B agent future
Conclusion: Building a metrics-driven AgentOps practice for production AI agents
